terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js signs Kofi in and sends GET /me with no cookie, with the cookie the sign-in sent and with a made-up one.

tasks.title: Make a token nobody can guess
tasks.description:
Implement `newToken()` in `src/tokens.js`. Each call returns a new session token:

- made from at least 32 random bytes from `node:crypto`
- written as base64url or hex text, so it can go in a cookie as it is: 43 or 64 characters
- never built from `Math.random`, the time or a counter

The check makes many tokens while `Math.random` and the clock are held still, and watches where their randomness comes from.
nextSteps: Read the lesson part on tokens.
Turn them into text a cookie can carry.
Run `node try.js` once the sign-in sends a cookie, and look at it.
hints: A token is only as hard to guess as the randomness inside it. The lesson says where good randomness comes from in Node.
`randomBytes(n)` from `node:crypto` gives `n` bytes nobody can predict. A Buffer becomes text with `.toString(encoding)`, and one of the encodings is made for URLs and cookies.

tasks.title: Start a session at sign-in
tasks.description:
When a sign-in works, make `POST /sign-in` in `src/routes/signIn.js` start a session:

- make a token with `newToken()` and save `{ staffId }` under it with `sessions.save(token, ...)`
- send it in a cookie named `session`, HttpOnly so the page's scripts cannot read it, with SameSite `Lax` (or the stricter `Strict`) and the path `/`
- the body stays `{ staff }`, and the token never reaches the body or the log
- a refused sign-in sends no cookie and saves nothing

The check signs in to an app with staff and a session store of its own, reads the `Set-Cookie` header and looks in the store.
nextSteps: Find the place in the route where the sign-in has worked.
Make a token and save the session.
Send the cookie with the options the task names.
Run `node try.js` and read the `set-cookie` line.
hints: A session has two halves holding the same token: what the server keeps, and what the browser carries back.
`sessions.save(token, { staffId: member.id })` keeps the server's half. `res.cookie(name, value, options)` sets the browser's, and its options are written in camel case.
`res.cookie('session', token, { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' })` before `res.json(...)`. The path is `/` unless you say otherwise.

tasks.title: Know who sent each request
tasks.description:
Implement `readSession(staff, sessions)` in `src/middleware/readSession.js`. It returns a middleware that:

- reads the request's `Cookie` header and finds the cookie named exactly `session`
- when the session store knows its token and the staff store still has that member, sets `req.staff` to `{ id, name, email, role }`
- otherwise leaves `req.staff` unset
- always calls `next()`, so reads keep working for everyone, and never logs a token

Mount it in `createApp` right after `express.json()`. `GET /me`, written for you, answers with `req.staff`. The check saves sessions of its own and sends `GET /me` with all kinds of `Cookie` headers.
nextSteps: Read the lesson part on reading a cookie back.
Find the session cookie's value in the header.
Look up the session, then the member.
Mount the middleware, then run `node try.js`.
hints: The browser sends all of a site's cookies in one `Cookie` header. Find the shape of that header in the lesson.
`req.get('cookie')` gives the header, or `undefined`. Split it at `;`, trim each piece, and split each at its first `=` into a name and a value. Compare the name with `===`.

With the token: `const session = token && sessions.get(token)`, then `const member = session && staff.get(session.staffId)`, then `if (member) req.staff = publicStaff(member)`, and `next()` in every case.
